Standard: The modeling, simulation, analysis tools, and databases for the evaluations of flying qualities characteristics and Levels are of appropriate maturity, fidelity, and accuracy to represent the air vehicle's flight characteristics for each combination of regions of handling qualities, air vehicle states, flight phases, and environmental conditions. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Review of the documentation to assess model requirements and development process, the fidelity and pedigree of the frequency and time domain-based analysis tools, models, simulations, and all the associated databases and components thereof (e.g., aerodynamics, stability and control, ground and ground effects, FCS and flight control laws, sensors, actuators, equations of motion, environmental conditions, terrain and ship models). Documentation is at the simulation level and also at the simulation subsystem level, to include subsystem models generated by the contractor (e.g., aerodynamic database, mass properties, equations of motion, force and moment accounting), and other subsystem models generated by subcontractors (e.g., propulsion system database, flight control actuator models). Documentation exists for all simulation environments used for Section 6 AW data generation, including all software simulations and HITL simulations. Hardware-in-the-loop simulation documentation includes time history, frequency response, and time delay comparisons with all software simulations and desktops simulations. Documentation includes limitations for use and any known deficiencies for the models, simulations, and tools, along with plans to correct them. Review design documentation to verify decomposition of air vehicle design requirements which define the required models, simulations, associated databases, and components and their associated levels of fidelity and accuracy to support the AW assessment of the air vehicle for each combination of regions of handling qualities, air vehicle states, flight phases, and environmental conditions. Review configuration control documentation to verify all of the above components for currency and traceability during development (e.g., preliminary design review, critical design review, test readiness review, first-flight readiness review, functional configuration audit, physical configuration audit, production), including incorporation of updates as a result of component testing, propulsion system testing, ground testing, and flight testing. Analysis.
  (1) Conduct a VV&A process, as specified in MIL-STD-3022, to show that the results created from the tools, models, simulations and all the associated databases and components are complete and representative of the flight characteristics for AW and SOF analyses. Verify and validate that modeling, simulation, analysis tools, and databases, which are utilized for evaluating AW criteria across the flight envelope, for all expected CG ranges and mass properties, for all flight phases, tasks and flight control modes, for all configurations and store loadings, and in the expected atmospheric disturbances for which the air vehicle is to perform its mission(s) are of sufficient fidelity and accuracy. The VV&A analysis should include: a. Model development reference documentation, the identification of the intended use of the model, the adequacy of the achieved model fidelity for the intended use, model limitations, model configuration variations used for different testing activities, and the model V&V approach. For example, landing gear and tire models should include, as a minimum, tire cornering coefficients as a function of slip angle, tire sides force, and braking force as a function of longitudinal slip. This data should be used in conjunction with aerodynamic effects on the air vehicle during ground roll. b. Model validation to experimental data or model verification to the actual subsystem or component specification requirements. When validating models to experimental data, an independent data set is used instead of a data set used for model development. c. The identification of the air vehicle subsystem key characteristics including performance (actuation system capacity), mechanical (hysteresis, backlash, break-out forces, threshold), and processing (data rates, latencies). d. Flexible air vehicle models included in the simulation or used for analysis are validated by ground vibration testing as well as airframe and control system structural coupling ground testing. e. The basis for demonstrating that the models (e.g., aerodynamic, propulsion, landing gear, and air data system) are representative of air vehicle ground and flight test results and uninstalled or installed propulsion system tests. f. Air vehicle simulation models used for mission planning or other performance predictions (e.g., fuel flow, climb and descent rates) are validated against the performance presented in a basic aerodynamic data and substantiating performance report. g. Uncertainty quantification for use in air vehicle flying qualities robustness analyses and simulations. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Examination.
  (2) Review of documentation as stated in Examination MoC (1) to verify all documents incorporate findings from testing and analysis results up to the conclusion of developmental test and evaluation phase. Analysis. (2) Conduct a VV&A process as stated in Analysis MoC (1) to verify all models incorporate findings from testing and analysis results up to the conclusion of developmental test and evaluation phase.
